Friday, 28 August 2026

Archive at Lunchtime August 2026: Programme 1

33 minutes

[ARCHIVE AT LUNCHTIME] HORSE PLAYS Notes by Sunniva O’Flynn Join us for free daily lunchtime screenings of films from the IFI Irish Film Archive. Collect tickets at IFI Box Office or online (with a small booking fee). PROGRAMME ONE HORSE In this melancholic rural drama set in 1960s Ireland, a widowed father (Mick Lally) is unable to communicate with his young son (Ruaidhrí Conroy) about their shared sadness. Dir. Kevin Lally. 30 mins, Ireland, 1993, Digital.

I Want Your Sex

90 minutes

When Elliot (Cooper Hoffman) lands a job with artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde), she announces that he will be her sexual muse, regardless of his current relationship with Minerva (Charli XCX). Initially relishing his new role as a willing sub to her dom, Elliot soon finds himself out of his depth. Gregg Araki’s first feature in over a decade is a frank and highly entertaining snapshot of contemporary sexual politics that challenges generational preconceptions towards sexual freedom. Notes by David O’Mahony

2026Gregg Araki

Bitter Christmas

111 minutes

After the death of her mother, advertising director Elsa (Bárbara Lennie) throws herself into her work before escaping to Lanzarote with a close friend, where unresolved desires and buried anxieties surface. Interweaving Elsa’s story, set in 2004, with that of Raul (Leonardo Sbaraglia), a contemporary filmmaker shaping her experiences into fiction, Almodóvar creates a self-reflexive, multi-layered meditation on how life provides the raw materials for artistic creation and the betrayals than can ensue, rendered in his unmistakably vibrant, primary colour-saturated style. There will be Open Captioned screenings at 13.00 on Friday 28th and 20.45 on Monday 31st. Notes by David O’Mahony

2026Pedro Almodóvar

Guggi

78 minutes

An intimate portrait of Irish artist Guggi from his anarchic days in 1980s Dublin with post-punk, boundary-pushing legends Virgin Prunes to his quiet life as a contemporary painter dedicated to the pursuit of beauty and the creation of paintings and forms that radiate calm. Filmed over two years in Dublin and Provence, and blending rare archival material and intimate interviews, Thuillier follows the artist in his studio, on the road, and in candid moments with long-time friends Bono, Gavin Friday, Jim Sheridan, and Sean Scully.  The 18.30 screening on Friday 28th will be followed by Q&A with Ian Thuillier, Guggi and his partner Gabriella Janni. Notes by Sunniva O'Flynn

De Gaulle Part One: Resistance

160 minutes

The first part of Antonin Baudy’s ambitious portrait of one of modern France's defining statesmen follows Charles de Gaulle (Simon Abkarian) from the collapse of France in 1940 to the emergence of the Free French movement in exile. Combining intimate character study with sweeping historical drama, the film examines the sacrifices, contradictions, and unwavering self-belief that shaped a leader in wartime. An engrossing exploration of courage, nationhood and the price of resistance. Notes by David O’Mahony

2026Antonin Baudy

The Odyssey

172 minutes

Although previous Christopher Nolan films have been grand in scale, this adaptation of the classic poem by Homer, showing exclusively on 70mm at the IFI, is of another order of spectacle entirely, harkening back to the swords-and-sandals and historical epics of bygone Hollywood. Following his victory against Troy, Odysseus (Matt Damon) returns home to wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) on a decade-long journey filled with incident. Notes by Kevin Coyne

2026Christopher Nolan
15:00

Tony

106 minutes

In 1975, on failing to win a writing fellowship, 19-year-old Tony Bourdain (Dominic Sessa) flees to a small town on Cape Cod with no plan other than to chase his high school crush Nancy (Emilia Jones). With no money and no accommodation, he lucks into the kindness of a local restaurateur he knows only as Chef (Antonio Banderas). Bourdain described his younger self in his bestselling memoir Kitchen Confidential as “spoiled, miserable, narcissistic, self-destructive, and thoughtless”, all of which is readily apparent, as is his charm and charisma in this enjoyable origin story from the director of Blackberry (2023). Notes by David O’Mahony

2026Matt Johnson

Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma

111 minutes

Kris (Hannah Einbinder), a successful young writer-director, is hired to reboot Camp Miasma, a moribund horror franchise in Jane Schoenbrun’s knotty, deliriously meta creation. Kris tracks down Billy (Gillian Anderson), the reclusive actress who played Miasma’s original final girl, to lure her back to the franchise. A deconstruction of 80s slasher movie tropes as viewed through a distinctly queer lens, with lashings of hilariously OTT gore, the self-reflective and intentionally artificial Sex & Death confirms Schoenbrun (I Saw the TV Glow) as a truly distinctive voice. Notes by David O' Mahony.

2026Jane Schoenbrun
